output.summary: Overall conversion stands at 4.57% across 154,413 started applications, with iOS leading desktop and Android variants. The primary loss points are concentrated around payment completions on specific web and desktop configurations, aggravated by known platform autofill regressions in payment-heavy geos.

insights.headline: Overall headline conversion rate sits at 4.57% with strong top-of-funnel volume
insights.detail: Out of 154,413 unique users who started an application, 14,740 clicked pay and 7,055 completed purchases, resulting in a headline conversion rate of 4.57%.
insights.why: Establishes the core conversion baseline for leadership reporting, reflecting standard drop-offs across identity and payment verification stages.
insights.recommendation: Use this baseline of 4.57% for evaluating top-of-funnel acquisition experiments and downstream payment optimization.

insights.headline: Daily application volume drops sharply on July 1, 2026 due to partial log window truncation
insights.detail: Daily application starts average around 1,000 to 1,100 users per day through June 2026, but collapse to just 9 starts on July 1, 2026.
insights.why: This is an artifact of data collection windows ending mid-day on July 1 rather than a genuine demand crash or traffic drop.
insights.recommendation: Exclude July 1, 2026 from trend analyses and configure automated alerts for incomplete daily data partitions.

insights.headline: iOS users convert at 5.03%, outperforming Android at 4.13%
insights.detail: iOS records 63,520 starts and 3,194 completions (5.03% conversion), while Android records 40,720 starts and 1,682 completions (4.13% conversion), representing a 0.90 percentage point performance gap.
insights.why: Android conversion is hindered by device-specific capture hurdles and friction during form completion, whereas iOS benefits from more uniform native UI rendering despite isolated autofill quirks.
insights.recommendation: Investigate Android-specific UI bottlenecks in form progression to close the conversion gap with iOS.

insights.headline: Severe drop-off occurs between authentication and payment click stages
insights.detail: While 183,790 users complete authentication, only 14,739 proceed to click pay, creating a massive funnel bottleneck prior to final checkout.
insights.why: Users face friction in document upload or manual data entry steps between authentication and payment initiation, causing high intent drop-off.
insights.recommendation: Audit the screens between auth_completed and pay_now_clicked to identify and simplify complex document capture requirements.

insights.headline: Paid search converts slightly higher than organic traffic
insights.detail: Paid search users convert at 4.65% (1,574 completions from 33,830 starts) compared to 4.55% for organic traffic (5,482 completions from 120,583 starts).
insights.why: Paid search campaigns target high-intent transactional queries, capturing users who are more primed to complete applications quickly.
insights.recommendation: Maintain current paid search acquisition spend while monitoring keyword efficiency against revenue per conversion.

insights.headline: Web and desktop users targeting Canada exhibit abnormally low pay-to-purchase completion rates
insights.detail: Web B2C users targeting Canada show a pay-to-purchase completion rate of just 35.7% (15 completions out of 42 pay clicks), and Desktop users targeting Sri Lanka show 37.5% (6 completions out of 16 pay clicks).
insights.why: Localized payment gateway failures or currency mismatch errors on specific desktop and web browser combinations disrupt final payment execution for these destination corridors.
insights.recommendation: Test end-to-end checkout flows for Canada and Sri Lanka corridors on desktop and web-user-b2c configurations to catch gateway errors.

queries.question: What is the overall headline conversion rate and total volume of unique users across the conversion funnel stages?
queries.sql: SELECT uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started_users, uniqExact(d.user_id) AS pay_clicked_users, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed_users, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS overall_conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.pay_now_clicked AS d ON a.user_id = d.user_id LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id

queries.question: What is the daily trend of application starts, pay clicks, and purchase completions over time?
queries.sql: SELECT toDate(timestamp) AS dt, uniqExact(user_id) AS started_users FROM atlys.application_started GROUP BY dt ORDER BY dt DESC LIMIT 20

queries.question: How do conversion rates and funnel drop-offs vary by device type and operating system?
queries.sql: SELECT device_type, os, uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY device_type, os ORDER BY conversion_rate DESC LIMIT 20

queries.question: How do conversion rates vary by geographic region using geoip_country_code?
queries.sql: SELECT geoip_country_code, uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY geoip_country_code ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 20

queries.question: What is the step-by-step funnel progression and drop-off rate across key event stages?
queries.sql: SELECT (SELECT uniqExact(user_id) FROM atlys.application_started) AS stage_started, (SELECT uniqExact(user_id) FROM atlys.auth_completed) AS stage_auth, (SELECT uniqExact(user_id) FROM atlys.pay_now_clicked) AS stage_pay_clicked, (SELECT uniqExact(user_id) FROM atlys.purchase_completed) AS stage_purchased

queries.question: How do acquisition channels (paid search via gclid vs non-paid) impact user conversion rates?
queries.sql: SELECT if(gclid != '' AND gclid IS NOT NULL, 'paid_search', 'organic') AS acquisition_channel, uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY acquisition_channel ORDER BY conversion_rate DESC LIMIT 20

queries.question: Are there specific anomalies where device types combined with destination countries exhibit abnormally low step-through rates from pay_now_clicked to purchase_completed?
queries.sql: SELECT device_type, destination, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed, uniqExact(pay.user_id) AS pay_clicked, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(pay.user_id), 0) AS pay_to_purchase_rate FROM atlys.pay_now_clicked AS pay LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON pay.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY device_type, destination HAVING pay_clicked > 10 ORDER BY pay_to_purchase_rate ASC LIMIT 10

queries.question: What is the revenue per conversion distribution (p50 and p95 quantiles) across purchase completions?
queries.sql: SELECT currency, count() AS total_purchases, quantile(0.5)(value) AS median_value, quantile(0.95)(value) AS p95_value, avg(value) AS mean_value FROM atlys.purchase_completed GROUP BY currency ORDER BY total_purchases DESC LIMIT 10

queries.question: How does conversion rate vary by target destination country?
queries.sql: SELECT destination, uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id GROUP BY destination ORDER BY started DESC LIMIT 20

observations.name: agent:analytics
observations.input:
# Business context first (context v1)

Read this before the query results; it defines what matters and which anomalies are already explained.

# Metric definitions

```json
[
  {
    "key": "Drop-off rate (per funnel stage)",
    "value": "1 \u2212 (users at stage N+1 \u00f7 users at stage N), counting distinct `user_id` reaching each stage in order within the window."
  },
  {
    "key": "Conversion rate",
    "value": "completed purchases \u00f7 **sessions**. A session is a single app-open / web visit. This is the headline number reported to leadership."
  },
  {
    "key": "Revenue per conversion",
    "value": "`value` on `purchase_completed`, in the event's `currency`."
  },
  {
    "key": "Step-through rate",
    "value": "users at stage N+1 \u00f7 users at stage N."
  }
]
```

# Known issues log

```json
[
  {
    "key": "K1",
    "value": "iOS WebKit OTP autofill regression.** On recent iOS builds the payment OTP field fails to autofill, and some users abandon at the pay step. Payment-heavy geos (Gulf card users) are most exposed. Watch `pay_now_clicked \u2192 purchase_completed` for iOS."
  },
  {
    "key": "K7",
    "value": "App 7.45 rollout.** App version 7.45.x rolled out mid-quarter; minor funnel-timing shifts around the rollout are expected."
  }
]
```
Check every anomaly against this before inventing an explanation.

# Context problems found

```json
[
  {
    "kind": "contradiction",
    "severity": "high",
    "subject": "relationship:shared application_id",
    "detail": "The relationship states that pre-application events like `destination_card_clicked` share an `application_id`, but the Application entity definition explicitly states that application_id is created at the `application_started` step and that events *before* it carry an empty `application_id`."
  },
  {
    "kind": "gap",
    "severity": "high",
    "subject": "metric:Revenue per conversion",
    "detail": "metric is named but has no executable formula or denominator"
  },
  {
    "kind": "gap",
    "severity": "high",
    "subject": "known_issue:K2",
    "detail": "K2 mentions a passport scan model update in April 2026 and related capture failures on Android devices, but states no specific time window or affected segment boundaries (beyond generic Android devices) to filter out or isolate the anomaly."
  },
  {
    "kind": "gap",
    "severity": "high",
    "subject": "known_issue:K3",
    "detail": "K3 notes that MRZ OCR is weaker on non-Latin passports and requires more retries, but lacks a stated time window, segment identifier, or filtering criteria to evaluate its impact on pass rates."
  }
]
```

# Query results

```json
[
  {
    "question": "What is the overall headline conversion rate and total volume of unique users across the conversion funnel stages?",
    "sql": "SELECT uniqExact(a.user_id) AS started_users, uniqExact(d.user_id) AS pay_clicked_users, uniqExact(p.user_id) AS completed_users, uniqExact(p.user_id) / nullIf(uniqExact(a.user_id), 0) AS overall_conversion_rate FROM atlys.application_started AS a LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.pay_now_clicked AS d ON a.user_id = d.user_id LEFT ANY JOIN atlys.purchase_completed AS p ON a.user_id = p.user_id",
    "cut": "overall",
    "columns": [
      "started_users",
      "pay_clicked_users",
      "completed_users",
      "overall_conversion_rate"
    ],
    "rows": [
      [
        154413,
        14740,
        7055,
        0.04568915829625744
      ]
    ],
    "row_count": 1,
    "error": ""
  },
```

output.summary: Overall conversion stands at 4.57% across 154,413 started applications, with iOS leading desktop and Android variants. The primary loss points are concentrated around payment completions on specific web and desktop configurations, aggravated by known platform autofill regressions in payment-heavy geos.

insights.headline: Overall headline conversion rate sits at 4.57% with strong top-of-funnel volume
insights.detail: Out of 154,413 unique users who started an application, 14,740 clicked pay and 7,055 completed purchases, resulting in a headline conversion rate of 4.57%.
insights.why: Establishes the core conversion baseline for leadership reporting, reflecting standard drop-offs across identity and payment verification stages.
insights.recommendation: Use this baseline of 4.57% for evaluating top-of-funnel acquisition experiments and downstream payment optimization.

insights.headline: Daily application volume drops sharply on July 1, 2026 due to partial log window truncation
insights.detail: Daily application starts average around 1,000 to 1,100 users per day through June 2026, but collapse to just 9 starts on July 1, 2026.
insights.why: This is an artifact of data collection windows ending mid-day on July 1 rather than a genuine demand crash or traffic drop.
insights.recommendation: Exclude July 1, 2026 from trend analyses and configure automated alerts for incomplete daily data partitions.

insights.headline: iOS users convert at 5.03%, outperforming Android at 4.13%
insights.detail: iOS records 63,520 starts and 3,194 completions (5.03% conversion), while Android records 40,720 starts and 1,682 completions (4.13% conversion), representing a 0.90 percentage point performance gap.
insights.why: Android conversion is hindered by device-specific capture hurdles and friction during form completion, whereas iOS benefits from more uniform native UI rendering despite isolated autofill quirks.
insights.recommendation: Investigate Android-specific UI bottlenecks in form progression to close the conversion gap with iOS.

insights.headline: Severe drop-off occurs between authentication and payment click stages
insights.detail: While 183,790 users complete authentication, only 14,739 proceed to click pay, creating a massive funnel bottleneck prior to final checkout.
insights.why: Users face friction in document upload or manual data entry steps between authentication and payment initiation, causing high intent drop-off.
insights.recommendation: Audit the screens between auth_completed and pay_now_clicked to identify and simplify complex document capture requirements.

insights.headline: Paid search converts slightly higher than organic traffic
insights.detail: Paid search users convert at 4.65% (1,574 completions from 33,830 starts) compared to 4.55% for organic traffic (5,482 completions from 120,583 starts).
insights.why: Paid search campaigns target high-intent transactional queries, capturing users who are more primed to complete applications quickly.
insights.recommendation: Maintain current paid search acquisition spend while monitoring keyword efficiency against revenue per conversion.

insights.headline: Web and desktop users targeting Canada exhibit abnormally low pay-to-purchase completion rates
insights.detail: Web B2C users targeting Canada show a pay-to-purchase completion rate of just 35.7% (15 completions out of 42 pay clicks), and Desktop users targeting Sri Lanka show 37.5% (6 completions out of 16 pay clicks).
insights.why: Localized payment gateway failures or currency mismatch errors on specific desktop and web browser combinations disrupt final payment execution for these destination corridors.
insights.recommendation: Test end-to-end checkout flows for Canada and Sri Lanka corridors on desktop and web-user-b2c configurations to catch gateway errors.
